briefings.title: A Script for Mark Zuckerberg | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: Meta is pivoting its strategic narrative to embrace its identity as an advertising and entertainment powerhouse, justifying massive AI CapEx by treating compute as a rentable asset that establishes a strict internal "hurdle rate" for ROI.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Meta is pivoting its strategic narrative to embrace its identity as an advertising and entertainment powerhouse, justifying massive AI CapEx by treating compute as a rentable asset that establishes a strict internal "hurdle rate" for ROI.

## Admitting Strategic Errors and Redefining Identity
* **The "Platform" Fallacy:** Mark Zuckerberg admits to a long-standing obsession with becoming a platform provider (e.g., Reality Labs, early mobile web efforts) which often distracted from Meta’s true strength: the advertising business.
    * **Reality Labs:** Zuckerberg acknowledges "burning credibility" with investors by spending 12 figures on VR/AR primarily because he thought it was "cool" and wanted to own a platform.
    * **Apple's Unintentional Save:** He credits Apple’s mobile ecosystem for forcing Facebook to abandon web-platform ambitions and focus on being an app, which inadvertently supercharged its ad revenue.
* **The Entertainment Shift:** Meta failed to realize early enough that "connection" was no longer sufficient; TikTok proved that social media had evolved into algorithmically-driven entertainment.
* **Affirmative Case for Ads:** Zuckerberg argues that Meta’s ads are a "force for good" because they generate new desires and connect entrepreneurs with customers, rather than acting as a "tax on search" like Google or Amazon.

## The Strategic Necessity of AI Investment
* **Existential Defense:** Everything digital is vulnerable to AI; Meta views massive infrastructure investment as a necessity to avoid "terminal value risk" and dependency on third-party AI providers.
* **Inventory Expansion:** AI represents the largest inventory expansion in history. By making "every pixel monetizable," Meta expects a massive top-line growth opportunity similar to the transitions to Stories and Reels.
* **Performance Enhancements:** Beyond LLMs, GPU-dependent machine learning is already driving content recommendations (keeping users engaged longer) and predictive ad targeting.
* **Addressable Market:** Because Meta’s products are free, the capacity to increase the top line through AI is unbounded by price elasticity.

## Financial Discipline: The Compute Spot Market
* **Selling Excess Compute:** To offset massive CapEx, Meta will rent out portions of its compute infrastructure on the spot market.
* **Establishing a Hurdle Rate:** These rentals serve as a financial benchmark. Meta will only "claw back" compute for internal projects if those projects can generate more revenue than the rental income would have provided.
* **Prescience in Spending:** Zuckerberg points to the 2022 GPU spending spree—which initially caused a stock dip but was validated by the launch of ChatGPT—as evidence that early infrastructure investment pays off.

## Meta’s Competitive Moat vs. AI Rivals
* **Connection vs. Productivity:** Unlike OpenAI or Anthropic, which focus on "work" and "replacing humans," Meta’s AI strategy is focused on "off the clock" experiences: connection, entertainment, and commerce.
* **The Hardware Opportunity:** While admitting VR was over-emphasized, Zuckerberg argues the groundwork laid by Reality Labs positions Meta to lead in AI-centric hardware (like glasses) that enables AI access everywhere.
* **Human-Centricity:** Meta’s core insight remains that humans are primarily interested in other humans; AI will be used to facilitate those human interactions rather than replace them.

> "Building a platform is antithetical to building an ad business. A platform’s goal is to feature third parties. An advertiser’s goal is to capture attention for itself." — Mark Zuckerberg

> "AI makes every pixel monetizable, which means we are looking at the largest inventory expansion ever... It will take a few years to realize this opportunity, but the technology is there." — Mark Zuckerberg

> "We are not out here to make chatbots or compete with OpenAI and Anthropic. They can fight for work and productivity... Our goal is to celebrate humans, to connect them, to entertain them, and to enable commerce among them." — Mark Zuckerberg

briefings.title: Fireside Chat with Yann LeCun, Executive Chairman of AMI Labs | RAISE Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: Yann LeCun argues that current Large Language Models (LLMs) are fundamentally incapable of achieving true intelligence or understanding the physical world; his new venture, AMI Labs, is developing "World Models" (JEPA) to bridge this gap, enabling robots and autonomous systems to learn from observation and predict the consequences of their actions.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Yann LeCun argues that current Large Language Models (LLMs) are fundamentally incapable of achieving true intelligence or understanding the physical world; his new venture, AMI Labs, is developing "World Models" (JEPA) to bridge this gap, enabling robots and autonomous systems to learn from observation and predict the consequences of their actions.

## The "Wall" of Generative AI and the Shift to World Models
* **LLM Limitations:** Yann LeCun notes that while LLMs excel at discrete symbols (text, code, math), they are "completely useless" for real-world signals and physical intuition.
    * **Predictive Failure:** LLMs use "auto-regressive prediction" (guessing the next token). This works for text but fails in video/physical reality because most world details (like the exact look of a person in a crowd) are unpredictable at the pixel level.
* **The JEPA Framework:** AMI Labs utilizes Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA), which avoids pixel-by-pixel generation.
    * **Abstract Representation:** Instead of "filling in the blanks" of a video, JEPA learns an abstract representation of a signal and ignores unpredictable details, focusing only on the underlying physics and logic.
    * **The "Cat" Benchmark:** LeCun points out that a cat has 800 million neurons (100x fewer than a human) but possesses far more common sense and physical intelligence than any current AI.

## AMI Labs: Strategy and Industrial Applications
* **Why AMI Labs Left Meta:** Despite support from Mark Zuckerberg, Meta’s internal focus shifted toward catching up in the LLM race. LeCun founded AMI Labs to pursue "Advanced Machine Intelligence" (AMI) independently.
    * **B2B vs. B2C:** Meta is a consumer-facing communication company, while World Models are best suited for industrial B2B applications.
* **Target Industries:**
    * **Complex Control:** Predicting and managing behavior in power plants, jet engines, pharmaceutical manufacturing, and human cell modeling.
    * **Defense and Robotics:** Moving beyond simple perception (image recognition) to "action planning"—allowing drones or robots to plan complex trajectories and manipulate physical objects reliably.
* **Global Footprint:** By design, the company has no presence in Silicon Valley or China, maintaining offices in Paris, New York, Montreal, and Singapore to ensure a global, independent perspective.

## AI Sovereignty and Project Tapestry
* **The Risk of Cultural Erosion:** LeCun warns that if AI assistants (the future "mediation" for all human information) are controlled by a few companies in the US or China, local cultures and languages will disappear.
* **Project Tapestry:** A proposed decentralized infrastructure for training foundation models.
    * **Sovereign Training:** Countries, universities, and entities can contribute local data and computing power to train a "global consensus model" without ever sharing their private data with a central server.
    * **Data Advantage:** This would allow models to be trained on vast amounts of non-public cultural and linguistic data (e.g., India's 22 official languages), potentially outperforming proprietary Western models.

## The Future of Physical AI
* **Data Bottleneck Myth:** LeCun dismisses the idea that we are running out of training data.
    * **Visual Wealth:** There are 20 trillion words of text on the public internet, but a four-year-old child sees as many "bytes" of visual data in their first few years as the largest LLM ever trained.
* **Achieving Level 5 Autonomy:** Current AI struggles with "common sense" tasks like inertia and gravity, which infants learn in nine months. Success in World Models is the prerequisite for Level 5 self-driving cars and domestic robots.
* **The European Opportunity:** While Europe "missed the boat" on the current LLM frontier, LeCun believes the race for Physical AI/World Models is wide open, providing an opportunity for Europe to lead through alternative research paths.

## Notable Quotes
> "LLMs handle discrete sequences of symbols quite well, but when it comes to real signals—video, sensors from industry or whatever—LLMs are completely useless essentially." — **Yann LeCun**

> "A four-year-old has seen as much training data as the biggest LLMs, except it's video... You learn that the world is three-dimensional. You learn that objects cannot disappear from one place and appear in another." — **Yann LeCun**

> "All of our information diet is going to be mediated by AI systems... If those systems are a handful of proprietary engines from a handful of companies on the West Coast of the US or China, this is the end of local culture." — **Yann LeCun**

> "Right now Silicon Valley is a bit in a kind of a trench that everybody is digging. They're all kind of working on the same thing... that’s an opportunity to seize for people who have alternative approaches like us." — **Yann LeCun**

briefings.title: From 'US innovates, China imitates' to 'Opportunity 2 0'  lessons from Summer Davos

people.name: Yang Yanqing
people.role: Director, ShanghaiTech’s Center for Education, Innovation and Sustainable Development

briefings.tldr: The global narrative has shifted from "China imitates" to "China innovates," as the "China Opportunity 2.0" emerges through leadership in AI and green tech.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The global narrative has shifted from "China imitates" to "China innovates," as the "China Opportunity 2.0" emerges through leadership in AI and green tech. Businesses and governments must now navigate a multipolar world where scaling technology requires balancing rapid innovation with job creation and energy security.

## The Shift from "China Shock" to "Opportunity 2.0"
* **Redefining China’s Role:** Aparna Bharadwaj (BCG) notes the old adage of "US innovates, China imitates, and Europe regulates" is obsolete. China is now a primary source of investment for the Global South and a leader in cutting-edge innovation.
    * **Corporate Sentiment:** Most Fortune 500 CEOs are looking to sustain or deepen investments in China, shifting from "doing business *in* China" to "doing business *with* China" globally.
* **The "Flywheel" of Innovation:** Yang Yanqing (ShanghaiTech) describes China’s success as a "flywheel" effect: combining large-scale markets with massive manufacturing to test and scale the frontiers of technology.
* **Ecosystem vs. Subsidies:** Yanqing argues that China’s advantage isn't just industrial policy or subsidies, but a state-supported infrastructure and a "nurtured ecosystem" that mobilizes social input into innovation.

## Competing AI Models: US vs. China
* **Funding & Focus:** The two AI superpowers utilize distinct growth models:
    * **The US Model:** Relies on capital markets and private sector resources to fund "frontier" Large Language Models (LLMs) and space-tech (e.g., OpenAI, SpaceX).
    * **The China Model:** Focuses on "vertical markets" and industrial adoption. Because capital is more limited, resources are scattered into specific industry applications where China’s massive data and manufacturing footprint provide a competitive edge.
* **Frugal AI:** Business leaders are beginning to discuss "Frugal AI"—the idea that AI should not be adopted everywhere at any cost, but rather where it is inexpensive and effective enough to provide a clear trade-off against human labor.
* **Open vs. Closed Source:** Yanqing highlights that China’s push toward open-source models may offer the Global South more agency in driving their own productivity gains compared to closed Western models.

## The Future of Work and Education
* **The Risk of "Jobless Growth":** Bharadwaj warns that the "technology economy" moves much faster than the "Main Street economy," creating a policy challenge for governments to prevent innovation from hollowing out the labor market.
    * **1-to-10 vs. 10-to-100:** Game-changing innovation (1-to-10) creates few high-paid jobs; scaling that innovation (10-to-100) is where mass employment is generated.
* **The Education Lag:** ShanghaiTech research identifies a "four-year time lag" in university curricula. While current graduates match today's market, the content they started with four years ago is already outdated.
* **Organizational Evolution:** Bharadwaj suggests it will take a decade for most organizations to fully embed AI into their workflows, even if the technology is ready now.

## Geopolitics and the "Global South"
* **Energy Security as Policy:** The conflict in the Strait of Hormuz has shifted the renewable energy conversation from an "ESG/Climate" issue to a "National Security" issue. Nations are diversifying into solar, wind, and nuclear to reduce dependence on volatile trade routes.
* **Supply Chain "Choke Points":** Global "choke points" (e.g., Strait of Malacca, Strait of Hormuz) are back in focus. Governments are now prioritizing "near-shoring" and "friend-shoring" to bypass these vulnerabilities.
* **Importance vs. Agency:** Bharadwaj notes that while the Global South has become "important" as "swing states" in a fragmented world, they must now convert that importance into "agency" by making themselves relevant to high-tech supply chains (e.g., semiconductors and pharma).

## Notable Quotes

> "One of the most common refrains you used to hear 10 years ago was 'US innovates, China imitates, and Europe regulates.' Today, I don't hear that anymore. China also innovates, China also competes, and China drives cutting-edge innovation." 
— **Aparna Bharadwaj**, Managing Director at Boston Consulting Group

> "In China's model... our focus in AI is more about vertical markets. Because we have more data and manufacturing spaces, it's easier for us to have breakthroughs in specific industries to create productivity and efficiency." 
— **Yang Yanqing**, Director of ShanghaiTech’s Center for Education, Innovation and Sustainable Development

> "How do you convert that importance to agency? Being important is not the same as having agency in the global economy... Global South nations are in a moment of importance. Whether or not they successfully convert it to agency will depend on the cards played over the next few years." 
— **Aparna Bharadwaj**, Managing Director at Boston Consulting Group

briefings.title: GameStop CEO Cohen Discusses eBay Bid, Video Game Software
briefings.tldr: GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen is aggressively pursuing a $56 billion acquisition of eBay, aiming to transform the e-commerce giant into a high-growth "live commerce" leader while slashing $2 billion in annual costs.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen is aggressively pursuing a $56 billion acquisition of eBay, aiming to transform the e-commerce giant into a high-growth "live commerce" leader while slashing $2 billion in annual costs. Cohen emphasizes his personal $500 million stake in the deal, framing it as a battle between a shareholder-aligned visionary and "entrenched" eBay management.

## Strategic Vision: Synergies and Growth
Cohen argues that combining GameStop’s physical footprint with eBay’s digital reach creates a unique competitive advantage in the collectibles and gaming markets.

*   **Physical Infrastructure as "Nodes":** Cohen plans to use GameStop’s 1,600+ locations (within a 15-minute drive of 80% of the population) as authentication centers to combat fraud in trading cards and tech.
    *   **Same-Day Authentication:** Shifting from a centralized shipping model to local store verification to reduce seller costs and buyer wait times.
*   **Live Commerce Expansion:** Cohen views live commerce as a $1 trillion addressable market (highly successful in Asia but lagging in the US) and intends to use GameStop stores as studios and logistics hubs for content creators.
*   **Digital Marketplace:** Plans to leverage eBay’s infrastructure to build out a digital marketplace for in-game items.
*   **Irrelevance of "Diskless" Gaming:** Addressing concerns about digital-only consoles, Cohen noted that software now accounts for less than 12% of GameStop's business, while collectibles make up over 50%.

## Financial Mechanics and Cost Reduction
Despite eBay’s rejection of the offer as "not credible," Cohen maintains that the financials are robust and the combined entity will be highly profitable.

*   **Aggressive Cost Takeout:** Committed to removing $2 billion in costs within the first year.
*   **EBITDA Projections:** Cohen estimates the combined entity will reach over $5.5 billion in EBITDA by 2026, including his proposed cost savings.
*   **Personal Risk:** Cohen is personally committing $500 million of his own capital to the transaction to signal alignment with shareholders.
*   **Financing Support:** Claims a "highly confident" letter from bankers (TD) and significant interest from capital markets, dismissing Moody’s "credit negative" outlook as a media-driven fantasy.
*   **Accretive Dilution:** Argues that while increasing GameStop's share count causes technical dilution, it is "accretive" because it enables the purchase of a business that can be scaled to "multiples larger" than its $56 billion valuation.

## Management Conflict and Shareholder Alignment
A central theme of Cohen’s argument is the disparity between his incentives and those of current eBay leadership.

*   **Entrenched Management:** Cohen criticized eBay’s board and management for "hiding behind advisors" and having "no skin in the game," noting the CEO makes $30 million annually without buying shares on the open market.
*   **GameStop’s Turnaround:** Pointed to GameStop’s Q1 operating earnings of $143 million—the highest in its history—as proof of his ability to manage distressed assets and ignore "mainstream media" skepticism.
*   **Direct Appeal to Owners:** If eBay management continues to refuse collaboration, Cohen suggested the decision will ultimately be left to the shareholders (the "owners of the business").

## Current Status and Next Steps
The deal remains unsolicited and unreciprocated by eBay, but Cohen indicates he is not backing down.

*   **No Price Negotiation (Yet):** Cohen stated he will not "negotiate against himself" by raising the bid immediately but left the door open for future adjustments.
*   **Proprietary Plan:** Refused to share a "codified" business plan on television to avoid tipping off competitors, stating the plan will be brought directly to shareholders in due course.
*   **Warrants:** Declined to predict the outcome of GameStop warrants expiring in October 2024.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "eBay is a platform that I can build into something much more profitable and much larger... It makes too much sense. So that's why I want to buy it. It's not that complicated." — **Ryan Cohen**

> "The business of live commerce is $1 trillion addressable market... The ability to go and use our nodes as studios and as fulfillment and logistics for content creators is huge." — **Ryan Cohen**

> "I want you to look your viewers in the eyes and tell them: Are you going to bet on an entrenched management team running the business or me, someone... risking their own capital? There's nothing more American than that." — **Ryan Cohen**

> "I’m not going to call my shots, but we’re coming for eBay one way or another." — **Ryan Cohen**

briefings.title: How NVIDIA Runs Its Own AI Factory | AI Factory Insider Ep. 2
briefings.tldr: Scaling enterprise AI requires moving beyond hardware to Enterprise Validated Designs (EVDs) that integrate the full software stack; NVIDIA’s internal AI factory demonstrates this at scale, processing 4 trillion tokens monthly and 200 million inference requests daily.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Scaling enterprise AI requires moving beyond hardware to Enterprise Validated Designs (EVDs) that integrate the full software stack; NVIDIA’s internal AI factory demonstrates this at scale, processing 4 trillion tokens monthly and 200 million inference requests daily.

## The Software Layer: Enterprise Validated Designs (EVDs)
*   **The "Five-Layer Cake" Analogy:** While Enterprise Reference Architectures (ERAs) cover the bottom three layers—energy, chips, and infrastructure—the EVD covers the top layers: models and applications.
    *   **Reliable Foundation:** ERAs establish the networking, compute, and Kubernetes layers.
    *   **Application Management:** EVDs define how agents, inference engines, and knowledge retrieval systems scale on Kubernetes.
*   **The Data Flywheel Lifecycle:** EVDs facilitate the full lifecycle of AI development:
    *   **Development:** Data curation, training, and model tuning.
    *   **Deployment:** Managing agent skills, harnesses, and production monitoring.
    *   **Continuous Improvement:** Capturing production traces and payloads to feed back into the next development cycle.
*   **Ecosystem Integration:** NVIDIA partners with Independent Software Vendors (ISVs) to create an "App Store" experience, providing "opinionated" full stacks where all components are pre-tested for compatibility.

## Scaling NVIDIA’s Internal AI Factory
*   **Massive Internal Adoption:** NVIDIA operates its own AI factory using EVDs to support 40,000 employees.
    *   **Volume:** The factory serves 4 trillion tokens per month with 99.9% availability.
    *   **Growth:** Internal demand for inference is growing at 40% month-over-month, totaling 200 million requests per day.
*   **Key Internal Use Cases:**
    *   **Chip Nemo:** A specialized agentic system used by 5,000+ hardware engineers for chip design. It handles proprietary file formats and non-public vocabulary.
    *   **IT Ticket Deflection:** Agents empower employees to self-service technical problems, moving from traditional support tickets to autonomous conversation-based resolution.
    *   **Knowledge Worker Productivity:** The "everyone is a developer" trend allows non-technical staff to automate workflows using AI agents.

## Security and the "Secure Agent Workspace"
*   **The Perceive-Reason-Act Loop:** NVIDIA defines the agentic workflow as a loop where the system perceives context (retrieval/memory), reasons via the LLM, and acts through tool calls.
*   **Secure Agent Workspace (SAW):** A reference architecture designed to run agents autonomously but safely.
    *   **Isolation:** Uses Virtual Machine (VM) isolation to create a "sandbox" for agents.
    *   **Network Perimeter:** Establishes strict policy enforcement around where agents run to prevent them from "running wild" or damaging adjacent systems.
*   **Confidential Computing:** A future-looking shift toward "zero trust" AI.
    *   **IP Protection:** Allows frontier AI labs to deploy models on-premises in an encrypted state that is "provably impossible to crack."
    *   **Data Custody:** Ensures the enterprise maintains full custody of inference payloads while the model provider’s intellectual property remains protected.

## ROI, Tokenomics, and the Move to On-Prem
*   **Drivers for On-Prem AI:**
    *   **Regulatory Compliance:** Critical for healthcare and finance where data mobility is restricted.
    *   **Tokenomics:** As AI projects move from Proof of Concept (POC) to scale, the cost of SaaS/cloud token budgets often makes owning the full stack on-prem more cost-effective.
*   **Measuring Impact:** NVIDIA prioritizes use cases with "clean statements of ROI," such as calculating engineering hours saved through automated customer support and ticket deflection.
*   **The Adoption "S-Curve":** Internal adoption typically starts slow during the pilot phase but spikes rapidly once tools are integrated directly into existing workflows.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "We like to say we're the only AI company that works with every AI company. So we've really gone through the whole ecosystem... and picked the ones that we know are going to run really cleanly on the AI factory." 
— **Nic Borensztein**, Distinguished Solution Architect, NVIDIA

> "It’s that realization where maybe historically you would have to hit the enter button all the time... to be able to do that autonomously but safely at the same time was really the breakthrough." 
— **Jon Fernandez**, Director, Enterprise AI Compute, NVIDIA

> "Infrastructure is real. The workloads are very real. It's no longer a question if agentic AI is here—agents are here." 
— **Kaushik Shirhatti**, VP, AI Factory, NVIDIA

briefings.title: Texas Governor Abbott, Saronic CEO on Floods, Shipyard Plans
briefings.tldr: Saronic Technologies is investing $3.2 billion to build "Port Alpha," a massive autonomous shipyard in Brownsville, Texas, designed to 1.5x U.S. commercial shipbuilding capacity in its first phase and address a critical national security gap.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Saronic Technologies is investing $3.2 billion to build "Port Alpha," a massive autonomous shipyard in Brownsville, Texas, designed to 1.5x U.S. commercial shipbuilding capacity in its first phase and address a critical national security gap.

## Port Alpha: Revitalizing U.S. Shipbuilding
* **Strategic Investment:** Saronic is committing $3.2 billion to develop a next-generation shipyard at the Port of Brownsville, focused on manufacturing medium and large-class autonomous surface vessels.
* **Addressing the Naval Crisis:** CEO Dino Mavrookas noted that the U.S. currently holds only 0.1% of global shipbuilding capacity, leading to a shrinking naval fleet. 
* **Unprecedented Scale:** 
    * **Phase 1:** Occupying 835 acres, the facility will provide 150,000 gross tons of capacity, immediately increasing current U.S. commercial shipbuilding capacity by 50%.
    * **Long-term Expansion:** The project can expand to over 4,000 acres, with a goal of reaching 2 million gross tons of capacity—a 20x increase over current national levels.
* **Combat Ready:** The announcement follows the first successful combat use of Saronic’s autonomous technology by the U.S. military (Centcom).

## Economic Impact and Regional Transformation
* **Job Creation:** The project is expected to create 10,000 new jobs in the Rio Grande Valley. 
* **High-Value Wages:** Governor Abbott highlighted that these positions will average $75,000 in annual salary, injecting approximately $750 million in total payroll into the state.
* **Macroeconomic Growth:** Saronic estimates a $160 billion economic impact on the region over the next ten years.
* **Industrial Shift:** The Rio Grande Valley is transitioning from a historically agricultural region into a "critical corridor" for high-tech defense and space, joining the ranks of major economic hubs like Austin and Dallas.

## Why Texas: Workforce and Infrastructure
* **The "Tipping Point":** While land availability and deepwater access were essential "binary" requirements, CEO Mavrookas cited the local workforce as the primary reason for choosing Brownsville.
* **Educational Pipeline:** Governor Abbott emphasized a multi-tiered training strategy involving:
    * **Texas State Technical College** for specialized technical skills.
    * **State Universities** focusing on real-life job skills and expanding campuses in the South Texas region.
* **Tech Ecosystem:** The proximity to SpaceX (Starbase) in Cameron County has created a collaborative environment where infrastructure and talent pools are shared across the defense and aerospace sectors.

## Operational Update: Severe Flooding in South/Central Texas
* **Emergency Status:** Governor Abbott provided an update on "massive flooding" currently affecting regions from Kerrville to Laredo.
* **Current Toll:** There has been one confirmed fatality and approximately 80 successful rescues as of the interview.
* **State Response:** Over 1,300 personnel, including the National Guard and Department of Public Safety, have been deployed with helicopters and boats.
* **Safety Warning:** The Governor urged residents to "turn around, don't drown," noting that the current rainfall totals are exceeding the record flooding levels seen in July of the previous year.

> "Our naval fleet is actually shrinking. We have 0.1% of global shipbuilding capacity. Port Alpha is going to turn all of that around... We will 1.5x the commercial shipbuilding capacity in the United States. And that’s just phase one."
— **Dino Mavrookas**, CEO of Saronic Technologies

> "The Rio Grande Valley has historically been an agricultural region... But now, with Saronic and Starbase, there is a massive explosion of economic activity. Our state is absolutely booming."
— **Greg Abbott**, Governor of Texas

> "This is built from the ground up to be the most advanced, to be the most efficient, but most importantly, add net new capacity, brand new shipbuilding capabilities to this country in a way that we haven't seen since World War II."
— **Dino Mavrookas**, CEO of Saronic Technologies

briefings.title: What racing reveals about working with AI — the OpenAI Podcast Ep. 22
briefings.tldr: AI is transforming professional racing from a "data war" into a battle of organizational efficiency, enabling smaller teams to bridge the resource gap by turning fragmented telemetry and human notes into real-time competitive intelligence.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
AI is transforming professional racing from a "data war" into a battle of organizational efficiency, enabling smaller teams to bridge the resource gap by turning fragmented telemetry and human notes into real-time competitive intelligence.

## Unifying "Hard" and "Soft" Data
The primary challenge in modern racing is not a lack of information, but the fragmented nature of data storage and communication.

*   **Breaking the Spreadsheet Cycle:** Much of the motorsports world operates out of massive, complex Excel files. OpenAI researcher Joyce Ruffell works with Chip Ganassi Racing to convert these legacy formats into AI-native structures that models can process more efficiently.
*   **Integrating Human Feedback:** While telemetry provides "hard" numbers (time-series data from ECUs), "soft" data—such as a driver’s description of how a car felt or a crew chief's handwritten notes—has traditionally been difficult to retrieve. AI is now being used to coalesce these diverse datasets into a single, searchable intelligence base.
*   **Real-Time Processing:** The goal is to move beyond retroactive analysis to real-time trackside decision-making, allowing teams to test hypotheses and adjust car setups between qualifying and race sessions.

## Democratizing High-End Engineering
AI serves as a force multiplier, allowing mid-level teams to perform at the level of industry "juggernauts."

*   **Competitive Parity:** Chase Holden, co-founder of RaceTek Systems, highlights that large NASCAR teams often have eight or more engineers on the pit box. Smaller teams use AI tools like ChatGPT and Codex to automate repetitive tasks, effectively "filling the gaps" left by having fewer staff members.
*   **The "Data Wars":** Holden describes the current state of racing as a "data war" where the winner is whoever can organize and interpret information the fastest.
*   **Bespoke Intelligence:** RaceTek focuses on "racing intelligence systems" that allow smaller crews to assess weekend performance through a smarter lens, ensuring no detail (like tire weight changes) is missed.

## Optimizing the Driver-Engineer Relationship
A significant hurdle in racing is the "communication barrier" between technical engineers and intuitive drivers.

*   **Digestible Reporting:** Drivers are not always engineers. AI is used to take four to five hours of technical practice data and condense it into "readable and digestible" reports that a driver can act on immediately.
*   **Informed Strategy:** By delivering insights faster, engineers can make more informed calls on the timing stand, ensuring the driver has the most accurate information during high-pressure moments.
*   **Human-Centric AI:** Both speakers emphasize that AI in racing is not about replacing humans with robots (autonomous racing), but about enhancing human performance. The sport remains compelling because of human stakes and "human-centric" goals.

## Operational and Logistic Efficiency
Beyond the race track, AI is being applied to the massive logistical undertaking of running a professional racing organization.

*   **Supply Chain and Parts Tracking:** Teams use AI to track parts that break or need replacement across global racing series, reducing human-error-prone administrative tasks.
*   **Business Management:** Chase Holden uses AI as a virtual assistant to manage sponsorship outreach, content opportunities for drivers, and complex travel schedules.
*   **Focusing on "Marginal Gains":** In a sport where victory is measured in milliseconds, freeing up a staff member's time from repetitive logistics allows them to focus on the "marginal gains" that lead to a win.

## The Future of Racing Strategy
As AI tools become ubiquitous and "Artificial General Intelligence" (AGI) approaches, the competitive advantage will shift from who has the tools to who uses them with the most creativity.

*   **The Power of Input:** Both experts stress that the "input" (prompting and intent) is more important than the "output." Success depends on a human's ability to communicate intent to the model.
*   **Instinct and Taste:** When every team has access to the same AI-driven data, the edge returns to the humans with the best instincts, the best "taste," and the ability to make a 10-second strategy call under pressure.
*   **Rapid Prototyping:** AI allows individual experts to "workshop" new ideas and prove them out quickly without needing to pull an entire team into a room, accelerating the cycle of innovation.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "It's always going to be about who can organize the best. The man and the machine—how do you get those to work together as seamlessly as possible?" — **Chase Holden**

> "Finding any gain is a remarkable feat. When people talk about the future of AI and robotics, I think sometimes they forget how many of the things we enjoy are enjoyable because they're human-centric. And I think racing is a prime example of that." — **Joyce Ruffell**

> "I believe we are in what's called the 'data wars' right now... every little piece of telemetry is, every little handwritten note, every idea, or every moment of strategy that's coming from a thought—you can catch that now and have it to implement." — **Chase Holden**

> "If you can come up with the idea, you can prove it out yourself much more quickly with the help of AI... you don't need to pull all these people in the room just to see if your idea makes sense." — **Joyce Ruffell**
